hints.title: Compare equations with zero on one side
hints.body: Move every term in each equation to the left, defining polynomials f and g. Compare their coefficients, paying attention to odd and even powers.
hints.recap: Putting both equations in zero form makes root-preserving transformations visible.
hints.pitfall: An outside multiplier changes outputs; a change to the input can move root positions.
hints.pause: Calculate f(-x), then compare it and its negative with g(x).

recall.reminder: Separate input transformations from output transformations.

hints.title: Test a root symbolically
hints.body: Let r denote an arbitrary root of the first polynomial. Use the relationship you found to determine the input at which the second polynomial must vanish.
hints.recap: An identity valid for every input transfers all roots, not just an example.
hints.pitfall: Check the reverse implication as well so you account for all roots.
hints.pause: Apply the resulting rule to the signs of the roots stated in the question.

recall.reminder: Use a polynomial identity to transfer information about every root.

solution:
Rearranging gives f(x)=x3+ax2−bx−c and g(x)=x3−ax2−bx+c=−f(−x).

Thus g(x)=0 exactly when f(−x)=0. The roots are the negatives of the original roots: two are positive and one is negative. Answer B.
